Latin word

prīvātus

prīvātus, prīvātī m.

noun (the adjective prīvātus used as a noun) · Declension on Wiktionary

a private individual, a private citizen; personal, private, one’s own (as against public or official); private, of one person, not of the state

In this lexicon

  • individual

    also used · classical · Tac. H. 1.49: major prīvātō vīsus dum prīvātus fuit

  • personal

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Sen. 22: in vītā etiam prīvātā et quiētā; Cic. Quinct. 15: rēs quae ipsīus erant prīvātae, his personal property (Lewis & Short)

  • private

    the recommended word · classical · Caes. BG 4.1: nihil prīvātī ac sēparātī agrī (Lewis & Short); Quint. 1.2.1; Traupman 178, 365; Traupman 291

Examples

  • manent ingenia senibus, modo permaneat studium et industria, neque ea sōlum clārīs et honōrātīs virīs, sed in vītā etiam prīvātā et quiētā

    old men keep their wits, so long as their interest and diligence last, and not only famous men who have held office, but also in a quiet private lifeCic. Sen. 22

    In the entry for personal

  • praesentem audīre mālō

    I’d rather hear it from you in personCic. Att. 2.12.2
